newsitem.title: UK: Iraqi officials due in UK for oil-for-food talks.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi officials due in UK for oil-for-food talks.

text.p: A delegation from the Iraqi oil ministry will shortly visit Britain for talks on selling oil for food and medicines as part of a deal approved by the U.N. Security Council, officials said on Monday.
A foreign office spokesman said the four-man delegation -- due to arrive in Britain on Tuesday -- included the director generals of the oil ministry's finance and distribution departments.

"The four Iraqis are visiting Britain to discuss legitimate Security Council Resolution 986 business to help the Iraqi people. All are connected with the oil industry," the spokesman said by telephone.
He gave no further details. A spokesman for the opposition Iraqi National Congress said one of the four was a representative of the Iraqi military industrial organisation.
U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan on Monday recommended a six-month renewal of the "oil-for-food" deal once it expires on June 7, U.N. officials said.

The current deal calls for $2 billion worth of oil sales over six months so Baghdad can buy food and medicine for its people, suffering from U.N. trade sanctions imposed in August 1990 when Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait.
About two-thirds of the monies are for humanitarian supplies, with the remainder earmarked for compensation of Gulf War victims and the costs of destroying Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.
